# Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood — Metacritic

- Original source: [Metacritic — Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood](https://www.metacritic.com/game/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood/)
- Author / publication: Metacritic
- Language / date: English page with German and Polish user reviews; dynamic listings checked 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: [Wayback Machine, 2026-07-01](http://web.archive.org/web/20260701214701/https://www.metacritic.com/game/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood/)
- Source files: `originals/reviews__metacritic.html` (earlier capture), `originals/reviews__metacritic.txt` (earlier text rendering), `originals/recovery/metacritic-expanded.browser.html` (19 recovered user records), and `originals/recovery/metacritic-critics.browser.html` (10 recovered critic excerpts)

The earlier capture contains seven critic excerpts and seven user-review entries. The recovered dynamic listings add five unique critic excerpts and twelve unique user-review entries, for 10 recovered critic excerpts and 19 recovered user records in total; 12 critic entries are retained after merging the recovered records with the original seven. The page says there are 15 critic reviews and 144 user ratings, so these recovered records still do not represent the complete historical listing. The two recovered user records marked as spoilers include full quote strings in the recovered data and are reproduced below.

## English translation

### Game overview

Roam the dense foliage of Sherwood Forest and come face to face with royal trouble as you fight for the common man in *Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood*. ### User reviews

Source for all entries: [Metacritic user-review listing](https://www.metacritic.com/game/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood/user-reviews/?platform=pc)

#### 10 — LT_Gruber · April 19, 2025 · PC

> Great and underrated game from my childhood.
>
> I really loved Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood. It is an RPG-like game in which you complete missions with Robin Hood and his team.
>
> In the beginning, Robin is the only character that you can play, but along the way you rescue your pals which then join your camp and are selectable for each mission.
>
> The story revolves around Robin coming home from a nice weekend with the boys on his Crusade, only to find out that his real estate has been robbed and taken over by the Sheriff of Nottingham.
>
> After a few missions, in which you wreak havoc amongst the Sheriffs soldiers, you find out that King Richard has been abducted by King Leopold V of Austria. Your main goal is to raise 100 000 pounds to rescue him.
>
> The mechanics in Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood are unique for the time. You play on a fixed map each mission and this map can be fully explored. You search for pouches of money, can kill, knock out or bribe soldiers, collect loot of bodies, gather information from the townsfolk or simply sneak your way around enemies.
>
> The combat is also unique. You get locked into a fight with an enemy and use the mouse to "draw" your attack in the air. When swiping from left to right, Robin or another character will attack with a swing from left to right. When drawing a line towards the enemy, the character will poke his weapon forward. It is just so much fun.
>
> All characters have different abilities and items. Some have a stick that always knocks out enemies, Robin himself has a bow with limited arrows to kill enemies.
>
> The graphics are gorgeous for the time. It is all 2D, but the environments are all nice and detailed and really give the medieval England vibe. The animations are beautiful and a permanent picture of how this game looks is printed in my tiny brain, along with all the other useless stuff that I know but don't need.
>
> The music is really calm and relaxing. It plays chill, medieval tunes that really enhances the experience when you drive your sword trough an enemy.
>
> The controls and interface are easy to understand and very accessible.
>
> The way you can choose your own playstyle and the freedom in which you can complete a scenario is what makes this game so much fun. I really enjoyed it as a kid and still do. This is one of those games that will always hold a place in my black heart.
>
> Definitely recommend this gem.

#### 10 — jacobredolig · May 18, 2024 · PC

I loved it as a child and played through it several times. It has not aged badly at all, if one overlooks that it does not run so well on newer systems. I would play it again at any time today; it has such a high replay value for me that it can only get 10 points from me. It is wonderful how you build a band of outlaws in your camp and send them from there to various places to complete missions. These places are beautifully designed, whether it is a forest road where a coach is to be ambushed, or one of the large cities where allies must be freed from captivity or even conquered. I love this game.

#### 9 — LoneWolfSones · July 1, 2016 · PC

> I recently picked this game up on a steam sale for dirt cheap and it holds up as well today as it did then. If you have played Commandoes before this game is very similar if not a bit more accessible. Robin Hood Legend of Sherwood presents an incredible level of freedom in how you choose to approach a given mission.
>
> Its controlled with simple point and click and you draw lines or circles to control your character's attacks. Its very simple and intuitive. It presents different characters that you can use to help accomplish your objectives each with their own skill set. Friar tuck can throw bee hives or put down flasks to get guards drunk. Little John can tie enemy soldiers up that have been knocked out and carry them to hide them. Robin Hood as you might expect has a bow that can activate traps, etc. He also can throw coins at the more simple minded guards to get them to fight with one another.
>
> Each map is incredibly detailed with the later ones that take place in castles being incredibly vast.
>
> I have read that there may be some compatibility issues so check to see if your current system or graphics card is supported. Its still a great game worth checking out and can be found cheap.

Source: [Metacritic user reviews](https://www.metacritic.com/game/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood/user-reviews/?platform=pc)

#### 10 — jacobredolig · May 18, 2024 · PC

Hab es schon  als Kind geliebt und mehrfach durch gespielt. Es ist auch gar nicht schlecht gealtert, wenn man mal außer acht lässt das es auf neuen Systemen nicht so gut läuft.

Würde es auch heute jederzeit wieder Spielen, es hat für mich so einen hohen wiederspiel Faktor, das es von mir nur 10 Punkt bekommen kann.

Es ist so schön wie man in seinem Lager eine Truppe gesetzloser Aufbaut, die von da aus zu den verschiedensten Orten geschickt werden um Missionen zu erfüllen. Diese Orte sind so schön gestaltet, ob nun eine Straße im Wald wo eine Kutsche zu überfallen ist oder eine der großen Städte in denen Verbündete aus der Gefangenschaft befreit werden müssen oder die sogar erobert werden. 

Ich liebe dieses Spiel.
